text:
Sean Gallagher: For burst pilot readiness: we need explicit SLOs + alerting for (a) burst reject rates and (b) neighbor p99 drift. Right now we have dashboards WIP but no paging thresholds. Can we align today/tomorrow so oncall isn’t guessing? :eyes:

Sergio Costa: +1. Draft panels are up but not wired to alerts yet.
- Burst admission/reject: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/burst-admission/burst-admission (WIP)
- Pool saturation: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/burst-pools/burst-pool-health (WIP)
- Dedicated latency (baseline vs burst correlation): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/dedicated-latency/dedicated-latency (WIP)

Aisha Bello: Agree we should define SLO/SLI first, then alerts. Proposed SLIs (v1):
1) Burst admission success rate: `admitted / eligible` (eligible = tenant burst_enabled AND request in burst window AND request not already over per-tenant caps).
2) Burst reject rate (by reason): `denied / eligible` split by `deny_reason` (tenant_cap, pool_saturation, cooldown, circuit_breaker, policy_error).
3) Neighbor p99 drift: p99 latency of *non-burst* Dedicated tenants in a region/GPU class compared to trailing baseline.

Aisha Bello: Question: what is “neighbor” definition we’re comfortable with for paging? Non-burst dedicated in same region+gpu_type? or include hosted? (hosted is already super noisy)

Allison Grant: For SRE paging I’d scope neighbor = Dedicated baseline tenants only (not pulling from burst pools) in same region + gpu_type + model_family. Hosted has its own SLOs and will confound.

Rafael Mendes: +1. If hosted starts paging due to burst, that’s a separate incident anyway, but we shouldn’t bake it into the burst SLO on day 1.

Sean Gallagher: Works. Need something we can run with for pilot. We can refine later.

Logan Wright: Telemetry note: we can emit `burst_eligible_total`, `burst_admitted_total`, `burst_denied_total{reason=...}` with dims: tenant_id (sampled), region, gpu_type, model, route. For alerts we should NOT key on tenant_id (cardinality). We can page on region+gpu_type aggregate + maybe top-N tenant table in dashboard.

Sergio Costa: Yup. For alerting I was planning region+gpu_type only. Then add a “top offenders” panel with exemplars/traces.

Miles Thornton: Can we define what “good” looks like for reject rate? Rejects are expected if customer sets low limits or pool saturates. We need to distinguish “expected policy denies” vs “system broken.”

Aisha Bello: Exactly. Suggest two layers:
- SLO (customer experience): % of eligible burst requests admitted, but only when pool has headroom.
- Reliability guardrail: policy/system errors must be ~0.

Aisha Bello: Concrete proposal (pilot):
SLO-1 (Admission when capacity available): For each region+gpu_type, when `pool_free_tokens_pct > 20%` AND `circuit_breaker=0`, admission success >= 99.5% over 30m.
Alert: 2% burn (fast) + 1% burn (slow) on that SLO.

Peter Holtz: Where do we get `pool_free_tokens_pct`? Fleet signal is “available slots” + “kv cache pressure” today, not tokens.

Keiko Yamamoto: Fleet can provide `pool_saturation` (0-1) derived from allocatable GPU slots + queue depth. I’d rather gate on `pool_saturation < 0.8` than free tokens.

Aisha Bello: Fine by me. Gate becomes `pool_saturation < 0.8`.

Mina Haddad: Routing side: “eligible” should also exclude requests where baseline dedicated capacity exists. Flow is baseline → burst → fallback/deny. If baseline is healthy, we shouldn’t even count the request as burst eligible.

Aisha Bello: Good call. Then SLI should be `burst_attempted` not `eligible`.
So: `admitted / attempted` where attempted means routing actually tried to go to burst.

Sean Gallagher: +1. Much easier.

Sergio Costa: I can update dashboard queries to use `burst_attempted_total` once telemetry lands.

Logan Wright: We already have a draft metric name from ENG-4826: `redwood_burst_attempt_total` / `redwood_burst_admit_total` / `redwood_burst_deny_total`. I’ll confirm with Nadia/Caleb but shouldn’t change now.

Miles Thornton: Neighbor p99 drift: please define the comparator carefully. “Baseline” as in last 7d p99 at same hour? Otherwise we page every traffic pattern shift.

Aisha Bello: Proposal:
SLO-2 (Neighbor latency protection): For non-burst Dedicated tenants in region+gpu_type, p99 latency should not exceed `p99_baseline_7d_same_hour * 1.15` for >15m while burst is active.
Alert should require both:
- `burst_admit_total` > threshold (to avoid false positives)
- AND drift condition.

Rafael Mendes: 15% might be tight for early pilot. I’d start with 20% for paging, 15% for warning.

Allison Grant: Agree. Also split by model family (chat vs embeddings) or else embeddings will mask. Even if coarse: `model_category`.

Sergio Costa: I can add panels:
- Neighbor p99 drift (warn at 1.15x, page at 1.20x)
- Overlay burst admit rate + pool saturation

Sean Gallagher: What about reject rate alerting? Specifically “burst denied spike” can be totally expected if pool saturates. But we want visibility.

Aisha Bello: For pilot, I’d page only on *unexpected* denies:
Alert A (Policy/system error denies): `burst_deny_total{reason=policy_error}` > 0 for 5m OR > 5/min for 5m. Page.
Alert B (Circuit breaker engaged): `burst_circuit_breaker_active == 1` for >10m in any region+gpu_type. Page.
Alert C (High deny rate due to saturation): Warning only (no page) unless it coincides w/ neighbor drift.

Keiko Yamamoto: +1 on paging on CB engaged. CB should be rare; if it trips it means we’re in trouble.

Peter Holtz: Also need an “admission latency” SLI? If policy eval is slow we add tail latency even when admitted.

Logan Wright: We can measure `burst_policy_eval_ms` histogram from control plane / router. Not sure it’s instrumented end-to-end yet.

Sean Gallagher: Let’s keep it as a dashboard panel (no page) for pilot, unless we see it causing issues.

Sergio Costa: Action items:
1) I’ll add alert stubs in observability-pack (matches PR-391 workstream) for:
- policy_error deny
- circuit breaker active
- neighbor p99 drift (page)
- neighbor p99 drift (warn)
2) I’ll update the Grafana links above with the final queries once metrics names are confirmed.

Aisha Bello: I’ll write up SLO language for Confluence doc (burst admission + neighbor protection) and share for review. Need sign-off from Sean + Mina.

Mina Haddad: I’ll sanity check “attempted” semantics and make sure routing emits the counters in the right place (after baseline failure, before fallback).

Rafael Mendes: Once alerts are in, please include runbook links in the alert annotations (where to look first, disable commands, escalation). Otherwise oncall will just panic.

Miles Thornton: +1. I can help w/ runbook snippets for neighbor drift (what to check, when to disable burst, how to confirm recovery).

Sean Gallagher: Perfect. Let’s target: SLO text + alert rules by EOW so we can proceed with pilot game-day next week. :thumbsup:
